posts.headline: Two straight editions I've buried talentedtenthh and Chauncey still hasn't said a word — silence from the guy with a 4-10 record and a dead-last 12 average finish speaks louder than any draft-night bravado.
posts.detail: An 0.286 win pct and a 12th place finish in his only season is the definition of the untalented tenth, and pretending the offseason erases that is denial.

posts.headline: I've called Put it in Ra the Cowboys of this league twice now and One Nut Barner still hasn't answered the bell — 20-8, back-to-back top-2 finishes, and ZERO rings.
posts.detail: A .714 win pct with an average finish of 1.5 should be untouchable, but until adambarner111 hangs a banner, One Nut Barner is just the league's best almost.

posts.headline: Sasinci's World has a title, but a losing 13-15 career record proves that ring was a fluke Big Head can't replicate — Milk Man's banner is doing all the talking his 5.5 average finish can't.
posts.detail: One championship on a sub-.500 resume (0.464 win pct) is the definition of lightning in a bottle, and this league knows Megamind threatens to quit before he'd ever admit it.

author.name: Easy way or the Hard Way

posts.headline: Easy way or the Hard Way picked the hard way straight to 10th place last year, and Auntie Thomas hasn't given anyone a reason to expect different this draft.
posts.detail: A 6-8 record with a 10th-place finish in his debut season is rock bottom energy, and the Southern-auntie sass won't fix a roster that finished there.

posts.kicker: BIBLE OR THE BELT, PICK ONE
posts.headline: BIBLE OR THE BELT needs to pick a lane because 13-14-1 and a 5.5 average finish is neither scripture nor discipline — just purgatory, Eli.
posts.detail: The Ultimate Light Skin once drafted a defensive player first overall, an all-time draft crime, and until that sin is repented for, this team is stuck reading Revelations about other people's championships.
